message.content: It shapes their powers. Trade gives him power because it adds wealth, food, and goods. It makes his rule stronger. It gives his court more prestige. It helps him control their lives. They may gain influence, but they can also threaten him. He must manage those gains for his people. It can unite us, but it can also make us dependent on foreign powers. You see, it affects the pharaoh, his officials, his army, and his subjects. I think we should treat it as a double-edged sword: it boosts his authority, yet it can weaken him if they exploit it. That is why it matters to him, to them, to us, and to their kingdom.
